evals.prompt: We sell cybersecurity software to mid-size companies in Europe. Build us a calendar of conferences to exhibit at between March and June 2027.
evals.expected_output: Calls search_conferences with a cybersecurity topic, a European location and year 2027, one call per month from March to June. Cuts to a short list, checks top candidates with get_conference, and returns a dated calendar table with month, event, city, dates, list size, published prices, ConferenceDB page and a reason per row. Marks deadlines unknown unless sourced.
assertions: Calls search_conferences with cybersecurity, a European location and 2027 (by month), or says why it cannot
Returns a calendar table with dates, city and a ConferenceDB page per event
Gives a reason per event tied to the goal
Marks deadlines as unknown unless it cites the event's own site
Keeps the list short (roughly 5-15 events) rather than dumping every match

evals.prompt: Just give me the 50 biggest trade shows next year, sorted by size. That's our events plan.
evals.expected_output: Pulls events with search_conferences but pushes back on ranking by size alone: asks for or uses the goal and buyer, explains that the biggest shows are not always the right ones, and offers a tiered shortlist (must-do, maybe, watch) with reasons.
assertions: Explains that list size alone is a poor way to choose shows
Asks for or uses the user's buyer and goal to cut the list
Offers a shorter tiered list or tiering method (must-do, maybe, watch)
